posts.title: TypeScript for Power BI developers: one 16:9 page
posts.excerpt: A coding agent can write a Fabric app for you. To check it, you need to read it. This is the TypeScript a Power BI developer needs for that, built up as one report-style page: a 16:9 canvas, two cards, a bar chart and a text panel over a DAX query.

posts.title: Upskilling for 2027: DAX and modeling are not enough anymore
posts.excerpt: Most of us write measures every day and almost never write a DAX query. But a DAX query is how report visuals, and more and more AI tools and apps, read data from your model. If you're planning what to learn in 2027, here's why I'd put reading DAX queries and a little TypeScript on the list, and where I'd start.

posts.title: Fabric app playground: learn to build one, in the browser
posts.excerpt: A playground in a browser tab for Power BI developers who know DAX and have never written TypeScript. You start with an empty folder and end with a report page on a semantic model. Everything is simulated, and the first step didn't work.
posts.question: Can an AI build a hands-on playground that a Power BI developer can follow from an empty folder, with nothing to install?
posts.tools: TypeScript, React, Monaco editor, esbuild, Claude Code
posts.lesson: The AI wrote all the lessons in two days and checked its own code after every step. It still couldn't tell that step one was impossible to follow. That took a person trying it.

posts.title: Gold Layer City: an anime opening, directed in chat
posts.excerpt: A 47-second anime opening for Gold Layer: a city built from code, three characters, and a theme tune made on my own PC. I directed it in chat and the AI wrote all of it. Twenty renders in two days, and what each one got wrong.
posts.question: Can I direct a full anime opening by chatting with an AI, without touching the code?
posts.tools: three.js, three-vrm, HyperFrames, VRoid models, ACE-Step, Claude
posts.lesson: The AI can build a city in an afternoon, but it can't watch its own video. It checks still frames. Almost every real fix started with me pressing play and saying 'that looks off'.

posts.title: Fabric apps: do you know what the AI is writing?
posts.excerpt: A coding agent can build a Fabric app from a prompt. This is the folder it starts from: what each part is, which files you edit, what each command really does, and the questions to ask before you ship one.

posts.title: Semantic Hub: ask your Power BI model, on your own PC
posts.excerpt: A small app that turns the Power BI models open on my PC into live dashboards I can question in plain words. A local AI writes read-only DAX, and nothing leaves the machine. What worked, what broke, and why the rules sit in code, not in the prompt.
posts.question: Can a local AI answer questions about a Power BI model safely, with every number coming from a real query?
posts.tools: .NET 10, React, ADOMD.NET, LM Studio (Qwen3 14B), Claude Code
posts.lesson: The AI is a query writer, not a source of numbers. What makes it safe is one gate in code that every query has to pass, and what makes it good is the model's own names and descriptions.

posts.title: Conversational BI: an alternative to reports, not a replacement
posts.excerpt: Asking your data a question in plain words is finally real. My take: it sits next to Power BI reports, it doesn't replace them, and it changes what a good semantic model looks like.

posts.title: Compatibility levels in Power BI: what each one unlocks (as of November 2026)
posts.excerpt: Every semantic model carries a compatibility level that decides which features it can use. This is a dated map of what each level unlocks, which features are still in preview, and what changes when the number goes up.

posts.title: Anime characters for our videos, animated by AI
posts.excerpt: Can 3D anime characters make our videos more fun to watch: a quiz short, the trailer, a race through the data city? Fourteen tests in two days: what worked, what looked wrong, and what an AI can and can't do for character animation.
posts.question: Can 3D anime characters, animated by AI, make our videos more fun to watch?
posts.tools: VRoid Studio, three.js, three-vrm, HyperFrames, Claude
posts.lesson: The AI wrote every line of motion code, but the parts that made it look right were human: the characters came from a real art tool, and every 'that looks off' came from a person watching.

posts.title: Pareto in Power BI: DAX measures or visual calculations?
posts.excerpt: The same Pareto chart built twice on Contoso data, once with visual calculations and once with DAX measures. Same numbers, different trade-offs, one ORDERBY trap, plus shaded ABC bands and a cutoff you can move.

posts.title: Know your PBIP: what every file in a Power BI project is for
posts.excerpt: A field guide to the Power BI project folder: what each file holds, which ones an AI agent can safely edit, and which ones must never leave your machine.

posts.title: PBIP explained: the Power BI project folder, file by file
posts.excerpt: The Power BI project folder in one tree: what each file is for, why plain text matters, and the few rules that bite.

posts.title: One row from CSV to a Copilot answer
posts.excerpt: The Gold Layer trailer follows one sales row through a Fabric data platform in under a minute. This is the slow version: what happens at each step, and why it's built that way.
